messages:
maya: FYI -- EU2 interconnect dropped ~30% cross-rack capacity from 03:10-03:24 UTC. I ran a quick admit/headroom check and wanted to get eyes on whether we should proactively lower admit to protect p99 during the next 2 hours.

maya: short summary: baseline observed throughput 120k reqs/min, avg tokens/sec per request 18, GPU pool effective slots 200 -> now ~140 after packet loss. p99 target = 300ms, p95 target = 120ms.

maya: quick calc I ran:
```
baseline_capacity_qps = 120000/60 = 2000 qps
post-flap_capacity_qps = 2000 * 0.7 = 1400 qps
observed_queue_build_rate = demand_qps - capacity_qps
if demand stays at baseline, queue grows at 600 qps -> p99 will blow out
Suggested transient admit = capacity_qps / demand_qps = 0.7 (70%)
```

maya: TL;DR: admit ~= 70% to avoid unbounded queue growth if traffic stays at baseline. Want to discuss whether to apply a soft admit curve (ramped over 5min) vs immediate drop.

drew: can you paste the actual demand numbers for the 03:00-03:10 window? did we see any user-facing error increase or only infra-level tail latency?

maya: demand 03:00-03:10 = 121.5k reqs/min (2,025 qps). Error rates: 5xx ~0.02% (network retransmits), p99 latency jumped from 250ms->420ms for that window, p95 stayed ~130ms.

sergey: math checks out. If p99 rose but p95 roughly stable that's queue tail amplification from a small fraction of requests hitting slower hosts/packets. Lowering admit to ~68-72% should pull p99 back under 300ms assuming homogeneous drop across nodes.

sergey: couple of notes:
- set admit curve with hysteresis: don't increase admit until backlog drains below 30% of target queue for 2 consecutive minutes.
- use per-AZ admit rather than global for eu2 so healthy racks can take a bit more traffic.

eli: +1 to per-AZ. If interconnect is the issue, global admit punishes healthy racks. We have metrics to split by rack in grafana: dash link https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops/eu2-interconnect

oncall-bot: incident: eu2-interconnect-high-latency triggered at 2026-03-18T03:12:04Z. Pages sent to oncall@redwood.com.

drew: operational plan proposed:
1) apply per-AZ soft admit = 0.7 target, ramp down over 2m (immediately start ramp).
2) monitor p99 across AZs and error rate for 10m.
3) if p99 > 320ms after 10m, cut admit to 0.6 and open bridge.
4) if 5xx > 0.5% or SLOs breached for >15m, trigger capacity-fallback -> route ~10% of EU traffic to dedicated eu-fallback pool (higher cost)

maya: cost note: fallback to dedicated pool ~ +$14k/day in burst GPU hours at current rates. But that keeps SLA-critical flows healthy. Worth it for a prolonged outage.

sergey: tiny nit on the numbers: dedicated pool can sustain 2500 qps when warmed, but cold spin-up is ~8m. If we plan fallback we should pre-warm 2 instances with autoscaler override. That cost is small (~0.6 GPU-hours) vs full fallback.

eli: I'll spin the autoscaler override to prewarm 2 instances in eu2 now.

maya: can someone write the admit patch? I have a snippet for the admit curve if you want to reuse: 
```json
{"policy": "per_az_admit", "target": 0.7, "ramp_seconds": 120, "hysteresis_sec": 120, "min_admit": 0.4}
```

drew: I can push the patch to canary (eu2-a) in 5m and watch the canary metrics. If stable we'll roll to other AZs.

maya: +1. please annotate the roll with reason: "interconnect degradation -> preemptive admit to protect p99"

oncall-bot: deploy ci/cd:admit-policy/1978 started by drew at 2026-03-18T03:32:00Z

drew: pushed to eu2-a canary. watching grafana. key panels: p99 latency per-AZ, queue-depth, admitted-rate, 5xx.

(10m passes)

drew: canary looks good: p99 down from 420ms->260ms in eu2-a, queue depth down 78%. No spike in 5xx. Rolling to eu2-b/c now.

maya: rolling notes: remember to keep the admit locked for at least 20m before increasing admit. We'll reassess after full roll.

eli: prewarm complete. autoscaler override set to 2 instances (eu2) at 03:36.

sergey: follow-up action: create a small retrospective runbook entry detailing thresholds we used (70% admit threshold, ramp 2m, hysteresis 2m, fallback prewarm), and add a synthetic to detect cross-rack packet loss patterns earlier.

maya: created GH issue: https://git.redwood.internal/r/infra/ops/issue/4567 with the runbook draft. assigning to sergey for writeup.

drew: thanks all. I'll leave monitoring on for next 45m and then revert admit policy back to normal with hysteresis if traffic/backlog healthy.

maya: thanks team :thumbsup:
